name_note: GTDB places this species in the split genus Blautia_A; the literature and NCBI name is Blautia faecis.

sentences.text: Blautia faecis is a strictly anoxic, Gram-positive, non-motile bacterium of the family Lachnospiraceae, isolated from a human faecal sample.
It uses carbohydrates as fermentable substrates and produces lactate and acetate as the major end products of glucose fermentation.
Another strain was isolated from the ascending colon of a French patient, and its 4.45-megabase genome was sequenced.
A newly isolated strain was selected as an acetate-producing commensal for use in the context of respiratory infections and tested in mice.
In one mouse experiment gavage with this species impaired cognitive performance, whereas Blautia massiliensis improved it.
